impact_en: Işık University publishes each term as one 1,301-row Excel workbook, leaving students to hand-check lecture/lab/PS clashes across hundreds of sections. IsikSchedule turns that workbook into ranked, conflict-free timetables: an admin uploads the term catalog once, and the web client returns up to 20 distinct schedules per request. The web backend does not run a metaheuristic — it runs one exact search (depth-first with minimum-remaining-values ordering, degree tie-breaking, forward checking and bitmask clash detection), then re-ranks the results with a quality-diversity (MMR) selector so the options shown differ meaningfully instead of being near-duplicates. Measured on 2026-07-25 against the live 2026-2027-Fall catalog, 3,367 solve runs returned in a median of 1.47 ms (p95 4.16 ms), and the backend suite passes 58 tests at 74% coverage with the solver module itself at 91%.
impact_tr: Işık Üniversitesi her dönemi 1.301 satırlık tek bir Excel dosyası olarak yayımlıyor; öğrenciler yüzlerce şube arasında ders/lab/PS çakışmalarını elle kontrol etmek zorunda kalıyor. IsikSchedule bu dosyayı sıralanmış ve çakışmasız programlara dönüştürüyor: yönetici dönem kataloğunu bir kez yüklüyor, web istemcisi her istekte en fazla 20 farklı program döndürüyor. Web arka ucu metasezgisel bir yöntem çalıştırmıyor — tek bir kesin arama yürütüyor (minimum-remaining-values sıralamalı derinlik öncelikli arama, derece eşitlik bozucu, forward checking ve bitmask çakışma tespiti) ve sonuçları kalite-çeşitlilik (MMR) seçicisiyle yeniden sıralıyor; böylece gösterilen seçenekler birbirinin kopyası olmak yerine anlamlı biçimde farklılaşıyor. 25.07.2026'da canlı 2026-2027-Fall kataloğu üzerinde ölçülen 3.367 çözüm koşusu medyan 1,47 ms (p95 4,16 ms) sürdü; arka uç test paketi %74 kapsama ile 58 testi geçiyor, çözücü modülünün kendisi %91 kapsamda.

adrs.title: Two independent clients instead of a shared solver package
adrs.context: The PyQt6 desktop client (first commit 2025-11-10) already carried 13 registered solvers behind a BaseScheduler abstract class. When the web product started as a separate repository on 2026-01-02, the choice was either to extract the desktop engine into a shared Python package or to let the web stack stand alone.
adrs.decision: Ship the web as an independent FastAPI + Next.js application with its own scheduling code. app/algorithms/ exists as a 'ported from PyQt6' placeholder but was never filled; the web solver lives in app/scheduling/solver.py.
adrs.tradeoff: Scheduling logic is now implemented twice and can drift apart — the desktop's constraint model and the web's scoring model are already different, and no shared regression suite covers both. Accepted because the web needed a different execution profile (one HTTP round trip) than the desktop's interactive metaheuristics.

adrs.title: One exact bounded search instead of porting the 13 metaheuristics
adrs.context: A web request must return a deterministic, explainable answer inside a single round trip over a 1,301-section catalog. Metaheuristics such as the desktop's genetic and particle-swarm solvers give different answers on identical input and are hard to justify to a student asking why a course was dropped.
adrs.decision: Implement a single exact solver — depth-first search with minimum-remaining-values ordering, degree tie-breaking, forward checking and bitmask clash detection — bounded to 100 discovered layouts and 20 returned, then rank with a quality-diversity (MMR) selector at 0.65 quality / 0.35 distance.
adrs.tradeoff: The API still accepts an `algorithm` field on POST /api/generate and silently ignores it (the parameter is bound to `_algorithm` and never read), so the contract advertises a choice the backend does not honour. The search is also bounded, so 'search_complete: false' is a real outcome on wide selections rather than an error.

adrs.title: Synchronous generation with an in-memory job map
adrs.context: docker-compose.yml describes a Celery worker plus Redis broker and a PostgreSQL database. None of it is installed: backend/requirements.txt contains no celery, redis or PostgreSQL driver, and app/tasks/__init__.py is a bare docstring with no Celery application, so `celery -A app.tasks worker` cannot start.
adrs.decision: Keep generation synchronous. POST /api/generate calls run_job() inline and the result is already complete when the response is written; GET /api/jobs/{id} then serves it from a module-level JOBS dict that is swept of entries older than one hour.
adrs.tradeoff: Job state is lost on restart and does not survive more than one process, so the deployment cannot scale horizontally without changing this first. Accepted because measured solve latency is a 1.47 ms median — a queue would cost more in moving parts than it saves in request time. The compose file remains aspirational and is documented as such.

adrs.title: Bearer JWT with a two-role check, and anonymous generation
adrs.context: The web release adds multi-user semantics the single-user desktop never had, but the core value — turning a catalog into a timetable — should not sit behind a signup wall.
adrs.decision: Authenticate with HS256 bearer tokens (python-jose) resolved by a get_current_user dependency, and gate admin routes with a second get_current_admin dependency that requires role == 'admin'. Generation, the public catalog and share-link retrieval stay anonymous; upload, friends, saved schedules and every /api/admin route require a token.
adrs.tradeoff: Tokens are valid for seven days and there is no refresh or revocation endpoint, so a leaked token stays usable until it expires. Anonymous generation also means POST /api/generate is only protected by slowapi rate limiting.
